terms.comment: Any place where things are made, from a smith’s workshop to a large works: Pliny has a fullōnum, a pictōris and a tingentium officīna (Lewis & Short). Name the product to make it a factory: officīna chartāria, a paper mill (Plin. NH 18.89, in M-O s.v. paper mill). Traupman also uses it for an office (see office).
Classically the workshop of a smith or other worker in hard materials, and also his craft (Lewis & Short); in comedy, a trick. Traupman’s word for a factory.
Greek ἐργαστήριον, found only in the late law codes.

phrases.latin: īnstituit officīnam Syrācūsīs in rēgiā maximam
phrases.english: he set up a huge workshop in the palace at Syracuse
a viper came into the smith’s workshop
